payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. An independent audit superseded and retracted the initial 12,000-cycle claim; the governing cycle-life figure is 8,400. The prototype’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh production scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry has a hard operating-temperature floor of 4 °C, below which the thalliline dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.

FLAGS: Source C conflicts on cycle life: “4,800 cycles” to the 80% knee versus “8,400 cycles” as the “corrected, governing cycle-life figure.”
VERDICT: REJECT - the audit supplies irreconcilable corrected cycle-life figures.
